changes.current_line: Proven ROI, backed by an independent economic impact study.
changes.change: For CFOs and finance leads: 'Send us one month of your statements and we'll show you what manual matching and unmatched deposits cost you, in your own numbers.' Have a solutions engineer work through it with their controller: staff hours at the customer's own cost, plus write-offs on deposits never matched.
changes.why: The deal went from 20 percent to signed when Wen priced manual matching from one month of the customer's statements and the CFO valued it as 'my number, not yours', the opposite of an independent study.

changes.current_line: Every payout reconciles automatically to its transactions and your ERP.
changes.change: For finance buyers at regional and B2B sellers, open the first call with this line, in their words: 'Know where every deposit came from, matched to its invoices and your ERP, without a week of month-end archaeology.'
changes.why: Payout reconciliation was the only thing that drew a reaction from the decider, whose first close took nine days. She spoke of 'the deposits' and wanting to know 'where my money is', never 'payments' or 'payout'.

changes.current_line: Financial infrastructure to grow globally, in every currency.
changes.change: Stop opening first calls with this line for regional and B2B sellers. Open with the reworked M9 instead. Also move M2 (developers) out of the first call when the IT team is not building anything.
changes.why: Dana ran the standard first-call deck and 'Silence was the whole opening'. Nobody on the buyer side said 'infrastructure', and the four-person IT team 'aren't building anything'.

changes.current_line: Support plans with tiered response times, up to 24/7 coverage.
changes.change: When the buyer is leaving a bank-bundled incumbent, lead with the person, not the tier: tell them who their named contact will be, by name, and what that person handles. Do not compete on rates. Confirm internally what can be committed before promising it.
changes.why: After the bank's only move was to offer to look at rates ('I didn't ask about my rates'), the CFO's new question was whether she'd get a named contact, because her bank rep had changed and she didn't know who the new one was.
